answer_text:
Let \(X=V/G\). Then

\[
X=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[V]^G,
\]

where \(V\) has complex dimension \(n\), so \(\dim X=n\).

1. \(\mathbb C[V]\) is a polynomial ring, hence regular and therefore normal.
2. For a finite group \(G\), invariants of a normal ring are normal: if \(A=\mathbb C[V]\), then \(A^G\) is integrally closed in \(\operatorname{Frac}(A^G)\).
3. Thus \(\mathbb C[V]^G\) is a normal affine ring, so \(V/G\) is a normal variety.
4. By Serre’s criterion \(R_1\), a normal variety is regular in codimension \(1\). Therefore its singular locus cannot contain any divisor.

Hence, if the singular locus is nonempty, every irreducible component has codimension at least \(2\). The exact codimension depends on \(G\); for example \(V/G\) is smooth when \(G\) is generated by pseudoreflections, while other finite groups give singularities of higher codimension.

\[
\boxed{\operatorname{codim}_{V/G}\operatorname{Sing}(V/G)\ge 2
\text{ (with empty singular locus/smooth case having codimension } \infty\text{)}}
\]
